title: MGA Entertainment Debuts New Music Video, Single Tied to Mirror Mi Doll Line (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All September 18, 2026 6:00am Mirror Mi music video MGA Entertainment MGA Entertainment has debuted a new music video and single tied to a new line of dolls dubbed Mirror Mi. MIrror Mi features six fashion dolls, each of which embodies “a signature emotion and brought to life through a distinct personality, point of view and style.” The dolls feature fashionable clothing, long rooted hair and collective accessories, among other features, that represent their particular emotion. They are: Blaze Maxx (electric), Amora Valentina (love), Luna Skye (dreamy), kiko Kittyama (crazy), Shai Meadows (sheepish) and Suki Goldpetal (fragile). Related Stories TV A 10-Year-Old Budding "Hollywood Reporter" Gets Her First Red Carpet Experience, Interviewing the Stars of 'L.O.L. Surprise! The Next Headliner' TV L.O.L. Surprise! Dolls Getting Their Own Live-Action Scripted Series (Exclusive) The cinematic music video “takes those personalities and emotions beyond the dollhouse and into an elite performing arts academy, where the characters (live-action) pursue their creative passions while navigating friendship, self-expression and change, ultimately discovering the power within every emotion,” the company said, adding that the launch “reflects MGA’s broader vision for Mirror Mi: using dolls as the first point of connection, then deepening character development and emotional relatability through music and storytelling.” The video was produced in partnership with London Alley Entertainment and directed by Grammy-nominated filmmaker Colin Tilley. MGA said that additional projects in the works for the Mirror Mi line include stop-motion films and an animated short-form series launching later in 2026. “With Mirror Mi, we set out to create a world as layered and expressive as the fans it was created for,” said Josh Hackbarth, chief marketing officer at MGA Entertainment. “The dolls are the first point of connection, but music and storytelling allow us to reveal so much more about who these characters are and the emotions that shape them. Every look, lyric and storyline uncovers another side of their personalities, giving fans another opportunity to connect and see themselves reflected in these characters.” The Mirror Mi dolls Mirror Mi dolls are currently available at retailers. The product line will expand with four-inch Mini Mis that can be customized, posed and displayed. “We didn’t begin Mirror Mi with a trend, a color palette or a silhouette. We began with emotion and feelings,” said Paula Garcia, chief design officer at MGA Entertainment. “That idea guided every creative decision, from the sculpt, expression and articulation to the hair, fashion and accessories, allowing each character’s personality and the emotion she embodies to shine through. To us, great character design does more than create something beautiful; it is about creating an immediate and meaningful connection. Every detail is intentional and every element has purpose, revealing something about each character’s identity, perspective and unique way of expressing herself. Mirror Mi represents our vision for the future of doll design: emotionally resonant, creatively fearless and unmistakably original. Watching these characters evolve from an initial idea into fully realized dolls and now seeing the world we imagined expand beyond the product and come alive through music and cinematic storytelling has been truly breathtaking.” The news follows on the heels of MGA, the company behind such brands as Bratz, Rainbow High and L.O.L. Surprise!, premiering a new live-action TV series tied to the latter, titled L.O.L. Surprise! The Next Headliner. The Mirror Mi music video is streaming on YouTube and the song also will be available on Spotify . Watch the video below. THR

title: Why Matthew McConaughey Doesn’t Want to Take a DNA Test — Despite Woody Harrelson’s Insistence — to See If the Two Stars Are Really Brothers
full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All September 18, 2026 6:00am Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey attend the premiere of Apple TV series 'Brothers' at the Hammer Museum on Sept. 17. Eric Charbonneau/Apple TV via Getty Images You may know the story — Matthew McConaughey ‘s mother once told him that she knew Woody Harrelson ‘s father right around the time McConaughey was conceived, creating a possible scenario where the two may be half- brothers . The rumor is now being taken to the next level with Brothers , an Apple TV comedy where McConaughey and Harrelson play versions of themselves who uncover a family secret that they may be related. There is, of course, an actual way that the two could find out the truth, as The Hollywood Reporter asked at the show’s L.A. premiere on Thursday if they would ever take a DNA test. Related Stories TV 'Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story' Team on Painting a Portrait of Female Rage -- and Leaning into Lesbian Theories Movies Zach Cregger on Revamping 'Resident Evil' and Why He Doubts He'll Ever Return to Comedy “I’ve been wanting to but he refuses,” Harrelson explained, as McConaughey replied, “I’ll probably come around to it” but added, “If it’s true, I got a lot to unpack. If it’s not true, he’s not gonna be near as fun to hang out with.” Harrelson admitted, “I’m going to be really sad for a while if it’s not true,” which seems to be McConaughey’s main deterrent to the test, as the Interstellar star joked, “Let’s just keep floating this idea, because I don’t want him being all upset.” Harrelson was quick to reply, “I don’t think that’s going to be a problem because I think we’re brothers;” McConaughey confirmed, “He’s fully convinced, I’m not. There we go.” #MatthewMcConaughey and #WoodyHarrelson share why they haven’t gotten a DNA test to prove if they’re actually related at the L.A. premiere of their new show, #Brothers pic.twitter.com/thzj17dLeH — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) September 18, 2026 The two stars — who previously shared the screen on season one of True Detective — also mused on playing themselves on camera for the first time. McConaughey said it was “More of an adjustment than I expected” and Harrelson explained it was “much harder than you would think, really. I was doing some weird, giggly, stupid performance and then I saw it and I was like ‘Oh my god, I hope we do reshoots.’ We did, so that was good,” teasing he told the director, “I don’t like that me, can we do it again?” Lee Eisenberg, who was behind Jury Duty and Lessons in Chemistry , serves as showrunner for the series, which sees Holland Taylor playing McConaughey’s mother and the pair’s wives and children also recast. “Their families would be there on the set, just hanging out at Video Village, watching versions of themselves. The whole thing was very surreal,” Eisenberg recalled, while also emphasizing that “I never wanted this to feel like a documentary” and the actors took some liberties to play up their personas. As for if he believes the two are actually brothers after working on the show, Eisenberg admitted, “I go back and forth. When you see the pictures of the two of them [from growing up] side-by-side, it feels a little uncanny.” Brothers starts streaming Sept. 23 on Apple TV. THR

The streamer is adapting the contemporary small-town romance into a TV show, which sounds like its in the vein of Netflix’s My Life With the Walter Boys and Ransom Canyon . The cast is currently being assembled with many lead roles already established. A release date has not yet been set for the series’ arrival because it is in early stages of development with casting. Watch on Deadline Has Prime Video’s Rose Hill TV series started production? Not yet, but as stated above, a cast is being assembled. Who will be in the cast of Prime Video’s Rose Hill adaptation? Jake Weary ( The Waterfront, Animal Kingdom) , Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway ( Under the Banner of Heaven ) and Sadie Dickerson ( Just In Time ) have been cast as West Belmont, Ford Grant, Rose and Skylar Stone. Jake Weary, Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway and Sadie Dickerson Courtesy/Kate Kondratieva/Calyssa Lorraine/Arden Dickson American model O’Pry is well known for appearing in the music video for Taylor Swift’s single “Blank Space” off of her 1989 album. Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado, and Curtis Hamilton also recently joined the cast. McGroarty will play Cora, Reid-Gantzert will play Emmy Belmont, and Mulholland will play Oliver Belmont. In recurring guest roles, Zumbado will play Tabitha and Hamilton will portray Bash Rousseau. Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland, Gigi Zumbado and Curtis Hamilton Who else is behind the Rose Hill adaptation at Prime Video? Is Elsie Silver involved in the creation of the series? Heidi Cole McAdams will serve as showrunner, which was revealed when Amazon announced the news of the adaptation at its upfront presentation in May 2026. Marc Webb will direct the pilot and second episode, and Temple Hill is producing. Silver also serves as executive producer alongside Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen, and James Seidman for Temple Hill. Temple Hill’s Annika Patton will also serve as a co-executive producer. How many books are in Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill series? The series consists of four books — Wild Love, Wild Eyes, Wild Side , and Wild Card . What is Elsie Silver’s Rose Hill book series about? The story centers rancher with commitment issues West Belmont and brooding record label owner Ford Grant, who are best friends and neighbors. Grant, known as Forbes’ “World’s Hottest Billionaire” has long carried a torch for West’s sister, Rose. Country-pop star Skylar Stone’s entry into the rugged mountain town setting causes ripples in the romantic family drama.

title: Japan’s Top Broadcasters Unite for First Joint Delegation to MipCancun (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Sep 18, 2026 5:00am PT Japan’s Top Broadcasters Unite for First Joint Delegation to MipCancun (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Japan’s Top Broadcasters Unite for First Joint Delegation to MipCancun (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Edmund Yeo and Vivian Sung Chase Malaysia’s Buried Past in Toronto Title ‘The Age of Goodbyes’: ‘Ordinary People Living Inside History’ 3 hours ago ‘Best of the Best’ Director Lena Khan on Making a Bollywood Fusion Dance Movie for Netflix, Working With Hasan Minhaj and Telling Maitreyi Ramakrishnan to Bring ‘Channing Tatum Energy’ 5 hours ago See All MipCancun Ten major Japanese broadcasters are joining forces for the first time to send a joint delegation to MipCancun , marking the country’s first coordinated television market presence outside Asia. The “All- Japan ” initiative is organized under the Japan Commercial Broadcasters Association (JBA) in collaboration with Japan’s Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) and the Broadcast Program Export Association of Japan (BEAJ). JBA represents commercial broadcasters operating television and/or radio services across the country, and the initiative is designed to promote Japanese IP and expand business opportunities across the Latin American content market. MIP Cancun is marking its 13th edition this year. Related Stories Richie Mehta on Turning Bandit Queen Phoolan Devi's Story Into a 48-Hour Siege: 'She Was Somebody Who Found Agency' How Irish Indie ‘Lemonade’ Landed Barry Keoghan in Between Beatles Shoots and Gave Him ‘Closure’ About Care System (EXCLUSIVE) The delegation includes Tokyo-based key stations TBS Television, Nippon TV, TV Asahi, Fuji Television Network, Inc. and TV Tokyo, along with Wowow Inc., BS Asahi, Tokai TV, MBS, Inc. and Yomiuri Telecasting Corp. A dedicated Japan Pavilion will be set up within the market’s matchmaking zone, giving each company its own table for meetings with Latin American buyers. Popular on Variety While Japan remains best known internationally for anime, the delegation will emphasize live-action content, particularly television drama, a category the Japanese government is now specifically targeting for overseas growth. “As IP development and co-productions become increasingly vital in the entertainment market, the industry is reaching a major turning point,” said Maria Perez Bellière, director of MipCancun. “We have high expectations for this initiative to introduce the appeal of Japan’s new content and firmly establish the ‘Japan brand’ in Latin American countries, with whom Japan shares a long history. We are deeply honored that Japan has united to leverage the unique Latin American market opportunities that MipCancun has spent 13 years building here in Cancun.” A “Japan Content Showcase” screening event will run Nov. 18 in the Cancun Theater Room, spotlighting programming from the participating broadcasters with a focus on Japanese drama for Latin American industry professionals. A networking cocktail reception will follow, giving the visiting companies and local buyers additional time to talk business. The push into Latin America comes as the Japanese government has named the content industry one of the country’s core growth sectors. Tokyo has set a target of expanding the overseas market for Japanese-origin content from JPY5.8 trillion ($37 billion) in 2023 to JPY20 trillion ($129 billion) by 2033, with a specific target of JPY0.5 trillion ($3.2 billion) for live-action content overseas by 2033. Latin America brings its own long history of serialized television drama, rooted in telenovelas that have been produced across the region since the 1950s and have traveled widely across borders. The continued growth of streaming in the region is also opening new pathways for international scripted content to reach audiences. Organizers frame the delegation as a way for Japanese networks to strike deals with Latin American buyers, distributors and producers when the market runs in November. MipCancun is a content market and conference serving Latin American and U.S. Hispanic television, bringing together acquisition, distribution and production companies to close content deals in the region’s growing TV markets. The Book of Mormon , with book, music and lyrics by Trey Parker, Robert Lopez and Matt Stone, choreographed by Casey Nicholaw and directed by Nicholaw and Parker, opened on Broadway March 24, 2011. title: Catalonia: A Dozen Highlights at San Sebastián, From a Time-Loop Thriller to a Singular Heist Tale and a Potential Arthouse Sleeper
full_text: Sep 18, 2026 4:31am PT Catalonia: A Dozen Highlights at San Sebastián, From a Time-Loop Thriller to a Singular Heist Tale and a Potential Arthouse Sleeper Catalan films also take in the latest from Isaki Lacuesta, a double San Sebastián Golden Shell winner, and a chance to catch up on co-productions , such as Berlin title 'Narciso,' and Isabel Coixet’s ’Three Goodbyes’ By John Hopewell , Rafa Sales Ross , Roberto Prieto , Callum McLennan 'Far From Trees' Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Barcelona’s soccer players packed out Spain’s FIFA World Cup winning team. Now Catalonia, the northeast region of Spain counting on Barcelona as its capital, accounts for a very significant chunk of the Spanish films playing this year’s San Sebastián Festival, one of its principal draws. Some 150 Catalan companies, no less, will be in San Sebastián. The bullish Catalan presence can be put down to an exciting new generation of Catalan directors and producers exploding on the scene over the last decade, since Carla Simón’s “Summer 1993.” Related Stories EbonyLife's Mo Abudu on TIFF Premiere 'The Secret Lives of Baba Segi's Wives' and 'the Consequences of the Decisions We Take as Women' Heartfelt, Rare Animated Belgian Feature 'Juul' Headlines Studio 100 Film's Expanding Slate at TIFF Market Key, also is Catalonia’s drive into pan-regional co-production, as many movies tap funding from around Spain. Also at play is a step-up in ambition among Catalan films at large and far larger mobility on the part of talent. So “Saints,” one of the big new Catalan films, is directed by Basque but Barcelona-based Mikel Gurrea , and one of the standout films by a Catalan director at San Sebastián, Carla Simón’s short feature “Flamenco,” is produced by Madrid’s Mamma Team. Popular on Variety Here are just some standouts from the far ranging Catalan presence at the 2026 San Sebastián Film Festival : Main Competition “5 More Minutes” (Javier Ruiz Caldera, Movistar Plus, El Terrat, Ikiru Films, Spain) ‘Five More Minutes’ Courtesy of San Sebastián Film Festival An on-the-rocks couple is caught in a time loop at a rural getaway. Part sometimes excruciating dark comedy, part sci-fi mindwarp and part suspense thriller whose grip bids fair to surprise at San Sebastián. Written and starring Berto Romero , one of Spain’s top stand-ups, playing opposite Belen Cuesta (The Endless Trench”) and an ineffable Javier Camara (“Talk to Her”). Spanish pay TV/SVOD colossus Movistar Plus, El Terrat, a Mediapro Studio company, and Ikiru Films, produce a typical genre cocktail for Romero, much directed with virtuosity by Javier Ruiz Caldera as a series of millimetrically calculated five-minute sequence shots. Filmax handles world sales. JH “Saints,” (“Sants,” Mikel Gurrea, Lastor Media, Nocturna Pictures, Deloris Films, Kino Produzioni, Spain, Italy) Courtesy of M-Appeal Played by Victoria Luengo, who starred opposite Javier Bardem in “The Beloved,” Lali cares for her dying mother Glòria, as she falls in with a gang who steals statues of saints, giving much of the proceeds to the needy and forsaken. Gurrea’ second feature, a step-up in style, shot with a continuous visual pulse, varying in tone from scene to scene. Produced by Barcelona’s Nocturna Pictures, Deloris Films and Lastor Media and Kino Produzioni, the latter two both behind Berlin Golden Bear winner “Alcarràs,” another exploration of an alternative economy. JH Special Screenings “Pray for Us,” (“Ruega for nosotras,” Daniel Monzón, Arcadia Motion Pictures, Ikiru Films, Spain) The latest from the still underrated Monzón, director of the breakout blockbuster “Cell 211” and the memorable “The Laws of the Frontier,” a five-time Goya winner that played out of competition at 2021’s San Sebastián. Set in 1974, after a night on the tiles, Ana, 19, is dispatched by her wealthy family to Spain’s Women’s Protection Board, a Francoist state-backed institution confining young women in the guise of moral “reform.” Arcadia Motion Pictures, behind the Oscar-nominated “Robot Dreams” and Sorogoyen’s “The Beasts,” produces. Picked up by Film Factory Entertainment for international, Elastica for Spanish distribution. JH Horizontes Latinos “Ashes,” (Diego Luna, La Corriente del Golfo, Animal de Luz Films, Inicia Films, Perro Azul) Lauded actor Diego Luna (“Y tu mamá también,” “Andor”) steps behind the camera to helm the adaptation of Brenda Navarro’s critically acclaimed feminist novel “Eating Ashes.” The film stars Anna Diaz (“La Cocina”) and Adriana Paz, who shared the Cannes best actress award with Zoe Saldaña, Selena Gomez and Karla Sofía Gascón for “Emilia Pérez.” The heartfelt drama trails Lucila, a young woman who leaves Mexico with her young brother to reunite with their distant mother in Madrid. Luna also produces via his La Corriente del Golfo label, founded alongside Gael García Bernal. Luxbox handles sales. RSR “Narciso,” (Marcelo Martinessi, La Babosa Cine, Guay Films, Bocacha Films, Pandora Filmproduktion, Bteam Pictures, Oublaum Filmes, Esquina Filmes, La Fábrica Noctura) Paraguay’s submission to the Oscars, the eight-country co-production “Narciso” began its lauded festival journey at the Berlinale, where it won the Fipresci Award at the Panorama section. Martinessi’s sophomore feature is set in 1959, where the charismatic titular performer returns to Buenos Aires at the height of a strict military regime. When the popular young man is found dead after a show, the culprit becomes even harder to find within this regime built on silence and fear. Luxbox handles world sales. RSR Zabaltegi – Tabakalera “Far From the Trees,” ( Meritxell Colell , Allegra Films, EXIT Media, Animalita Cine, Spain) A Locarno 2026 Fipresci Prize winner. Adela, a sound artist recording endangered languages travels to the Peruvian highlands in a film which weaves present and past – collective and personal memory and archive footage of the Catalan diaspora after the Spanish Civil War – speaking about family, forced exile, roots, memory and hybrid identity. “A richly contemplative journey of physical and mental meanderings, beautifully combining 4K digital with Super 16,” says Variety. “Ambitious in scope yet intimate in focus,” Far From the Trees” “could well become an arthouse sleeper,” it adds. JH “Flamenco Sketches,” (“Jaleos,” Isaki Lacuesta , Lastor Media, Goroka Contents, with La Termita Films, Spain) Courtesy of San Sebastián Film Festival Sharing with Francis Ford Coppola the rare honour of two San Sebastián Golden Shells, Isaki Lacuesta returns to the festival fresh from co-directing HBO Max’s acclaimed series “Ravalear.” “Flamenco Sketches” is a restless ride through cinema, machines, Nazism, Civil War, and avant-garde art. The film shows how flamenco has often swallowed disruption whole only to morph itself anew. “Always dying, never dead.” one of the many contributing voices in the doc tells us. CM “Red Rocks,” (Bruno Dumont, Rosa Filmes, Luxbox, Nightswim, Andergraun Films, Tessalit, Pulpa Films, Sula Films) The latest by the Silver Bear winner of “The Empire” premiered at Directors’ Fortnight in Cannes and tells the tale of two gangs of kids who compete in the dangerous game of cliff jumping in the French Riviera. Dumont worked with a cast of non-professional actors, adopting a documentary-like approach to the film, shot against the cliffs and open waters of the Mediterranean. The lauded director won two Grand Prix awards at Cannes for “Humanity” and “Flanders.” Luxbox handles world sales. RSR Made in Spain “Alive” (“Viva” Aina Clotet, Ikiru Films, Funicular Films, La Terraza Films) In the intimate “Viva,” which earned its director-star Clotet the Louis Roederer Foundation Rising Star Award, follows 40-something Nora as she finds a new lease of life following cancer treatment. The heartfelt drama explores relationships, as well as the dilemmas brought in by climate change, with a standout performance by the established Clotet, whose 2024 series “This is Not Sweden” racked up several awards and found great success with audiences. The director produces under her Funicular Films label, alongside veteran Edmon Roch of Ikiru Films. Loco Films handles sales, while Caramel Films distributes in Spain. RSR “The Good Daughter,” (Astra Pictures, Avalon, Krater, Spain, Belgium) The sophomore feature of Julia de Paz Solvas, also a co-writer on Alauda Ruiz de Azúa’s “Querer,” plumbing gender violence from the untutored perspective of Carmela, the daughter of a direct victim. A trenchant portrait of self pitying, violent male narcissism and an uplifting take on teen female friendship which swept the Tallinn Black Nights Festival in November, sweeping its Grand Prix, actress (Kiara Arancibia) and Audience Awards. JH “Sixteen Moments of My Life” (Albert Serra, Idéale Audience, Andergraun Films, Weltfilm, Spain, France, Germany) The latest by irreverent Catalan maverick Albert Serra (“Pacifiction,” “Afternoons of Solitude”) premiered at Locarno. It documents a one-off performance by legendary German film actress and singer Ingrid Caven – known for her collaborations with then-husband Rainer Werner Fassbinder – at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris. Neither a biopic nor a concert movie, “Sixteen Moments of My Life” puts forward a fascinating portrayal of creatives on creatives. Serra’s Andergraun Films label produces and handles sales. RSR “Three Goodbyes,” ( Isabel Coixet , Cattleya, Ruvido Produzioni, Bartlebyfilm, Buena Pinta Media, Vision Distribution, Bteam Prods, Perdición Films, Tres Cuencos, Apaches Entertainment, Spain, Italy) Bowing at least year’s Toronto, a home-run from Isabel Coixet, Adapting a short story collection by Italy’s Michela Murgia, who died of cancer at 51. Alba Rohrwacher “dazzles in a humane, heartfelt drama” as the “luminous center of a charmingly bittersweet and life-affirming movie,” Variety wrote. “In other hands, this would cue a standard disease-of-the-week weepie, but Coixet keeps the tone lightly wistful and wise,” it added. title: Catalonia’s New Generation Raises Its Game as Ambition, Scale and Genre Drive Bolder Arthouse and Crossover Titles
full_text: Sep 18, 2026 4:17am PT Catalonia’s New Generation Raises Its Game as Ambition, Scale and Genre Drive Bolder Arthouse and Crossover Titles Key emerging Catalan filmmakers at San Sebastián – Berto Romero, Mikel Gurrea, Meritxell Colell, Aina Clotet – are raising their game, in larger scale, genre blending, visual ambition and more involved storytelling. They have very good reason By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest Catalonia: A Dozen Highlights at San Sebastián, From a Time-Loop Thriller to a Singular Heist Tale and a Potential Arthouse Sleeper 2 hours ago Catalonia’s New Generation Raises Its Game as Ambition, Scale and Genre Drive Bolder Arthouse and Crossover Titles 2 hours ago Oscars: Spain Selects ‘La Bola Negra’ for International Feature Race 2 days ago See All 'Five More Minutes' Courtesy of San Sebastián Film Festival Over 2019-25, annual Catalan government general cinema funding soared from €12.5 million ($14.4 million) in 2019 to €30.2 million ($34.8 million) in just specific support lines. Now, however, the films that are being made are also getting bigger, as a new generation of filmmakers and TV creatives emerged over the last decade raise their game in their artistic ambitions and production values. Related Stories Chase Infiniti on TIFF Breakout ‘The Julia Set,’ Love Bombing and Music Video Stardom Jorge Alonso's Spanish Romance Drama 'All That We Never Were' Sells to France and India (EXCLUSIVE) New movies at San Sebastián from rapidly consolidating Catalan or Catalonia-based writers and directors is a case in point. Mikel Gurrea’s main competition player “Saints,” for example, launches as a mini visual mystery thriller. Distant lights – maybe car lights or fireflies – dance across a pitch-black night scene. They are finally revealed as the head-lamps of a gang of thieves, robbing a church, caught closer up, their faces occasionally emerging from the gloom. Popular on Variety Cleverly, in visual terms, not dialog, Gurrea not just launches the film but anticipates its focus: This is an identity drama, this focus becoming how late-20s Lali establishes her priorities, between a chosen family – an elite band of church artefacts thieves – and her biological family, her dying mother. “Saints’” budget is “roughly twice” that of “Suro,” Gurrea’s 2022 debut which also competed at San Sebastián, says “Saints” producer Laura Rubirola Salas. That budget spike can be put down to spiraling production costs and a film “more complex in terms of locations, number of characters and overall production values,” she adds. Written and starring Berto Romero , “5 More Minutes” delivers a reportedly excruciatingly comedic sci-fi thriller as an on-the-rocks couple are caught in a time loop at a rural getaway. Suddenly, a world of normal multi-shot set-ups morphs into one of millimetrically calculated five-minute sequence shots, film at the same time of 6.35 p.m. to achieve similar light conditions. None of which as an easy task. 2018’s “Land of Loneliness” (“Con el viento”), Meritxell Colell ’s first fiction feature, unspooled in a Spanish village. Her third, “Far From the Trees,” one of Locarno biggest winners this August, begins in the Amazon jungle, so0n moves to Peru’s highlands, following Adela, a sound artist recording endangered languages. The locations can be eye-catching. What quickly dazzles, however, is an intricate mix of present and past, collective and personal memory, of the archive footage of the Catalan diaspora after the Spanish Civil War and scenes of Adela as a child, and a present in a film which speaks about family, forced exile, roots, memory and identity. Why the Step-Up in Ambition? Aiming to raise the ante in style and scale, cineastes are emboldened by success, theirs and of others. Over the last decade, Catalan productions have won Best First Feature (“Summer 1993”), a Golden Bear (Alcarràs,” also from Carla Simón) and Best Leading Performance (“20,000 Species of Bees”) at the Berlin Film Festival. “Sirāt” took a Cannes Jury Prize last year, and two Academy Award nominations. Smaller films have also triumphed: “The Good Daughter,” now playing at San Sebastián, scooped top prizes at Tallinn Black Nights Festival, last year; “Forastera,” directed by Lucía Aleñar Iglesias, won a Fipresci Prize at 2025’s Toronto. In a more commercial way of things, Paramount Pictures is giving a theatrical release to “Tad and the Magic Lamp,” part of the animated movie series, in over 40 international territories, including nearly all major markets around the world, notes producer Edmon Roch. Another film he co-produced, Aina Clotet’s “Alive” (“Viva”), now at San Sebastián, won the 2026 Cannes Critics’ Week’s Louis Roederer Foundation Rising Star Award. “Nobody sets out to make a bigger film, that isn’t the place we create from,” says Colell. So she wrote “Far from the Trees” “freely, without thinking if the film could be made, pouring in cinematographic, emotional and narratives desires.” That said, she is “less afraid of taking risks” thanks to a growing confidence of her own capacities and those of key collaborators, such as editor Ana Pfaff, who has also edited Clara Simón’s films including the sensational short “Flamenco,” set to screen at San Sebastián. “Suro’s”success gave us the confidence to make a film that could once again compete in the Official Selection of a major festival like San Sebastián, and travel internationally without any complexes. I feel this is something we question less and less,” Rubirola Salas says, talking about Gurrea’s debut. Also, the money’s there. In 2025, Spain produced 435 features, more than any other country in Europe. That speaks large, in part, to the emergence of consolidated regional firm industries such as Catalonia’s. But Spain’s regions do not finance films on their own. “Far From the Trees” worked a “fundamental” national-regional axis, says Colell, tapping finance from Spain’s national ICAA film agency and the Catalan Government ICEC. “5 More Minutes” benefitted from co-production by Movistar Plus, the biggest Spanish pay TV/SVOD operator, which set out from its first announced slate in 2023 to make auteur event movies at budgets competitive with similar movies in , say, France. Spain, and most especially Catalonia, which boasts a minority co-production fund, furthermore ranks with Belgium among the easiest of co-producer partner countries in Europe. And success breeds success. The relationship between Lastor Media and Italy’s Kino Produzioni, forged on “Alcarràs,” now both producers on “Saints,” has been “key to expanding our financing capacity,” says Rubirola Salas. Also, in producing more original films, which push the envelope on narrative or visuals, filmmakers are making a virtue out of a market necessity. Bolder films made at higher production standards is one way to stand out from the crowd. “Films have to be very competitive these days. We are releasing them in the same conditions as the rest of the films in the world. Filmmakers realize that it’s not enough to just have good ideas,. They also need great ambitions and to show them,” says Roch. That includes first-time feature directors. Roch cites “Alive” (“Viva”), made by Clotet, bulwarked in confidence by her breakout groundbreaking international TV co-production “This Is Not Sweden.” An issue-blender, it turns on Nora, 40, who plunges into a relationship with a much younger man. Also, she faces possibly recurrent breast cancer and a world desiccated by global warming. Another case in point, Roch says, is “5 More Minutes.” Romero had just made for Movistar Plus the TV series hit “The Other Side,” which confirmed his ability to juggle genre – there horror, comedy and a thriller propulsion. Movistar Plus was “very comfortable with Berto making a first feature, was with us from the very start and made it possible for us to have the elements we needed to make it,” says Roch. “The idea is to get great stories and then just power them up across the board in all their different elements to have international stories that they can travel very well.” Tom Hanks, Ta-Nehisi Coates and More Join Barack Obama’s ‘A Great Book’ Podcast at Audible Like Nastya Signs Content Development Deal With Disney Alfonso Cuaron to Make First Korea Visit at Busan as Festival Also Spotlights European Women+ Filmmakers San Sebastián 2026: ‘Les Mis,’ Los Javis, Brad Pitt, Penélope Cruz and Much More ‘Heated Rivalry’ Star Hudson Williams Sparks TIFF Chaos, Teases Season 2 Rei Ami on Her New Pop Girl Era, and How Feeling Confident Inspired Her New Single ‘2 Loud’: ‘It’s a Clapback’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... title: International Oscar Submissions: Spain, Indonesia, Hungary, Nepal, Israel and More Join the List
full_text: ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection The campaigns for the Oscar for international feature film are gaining momentum, with final submissions due by Oct. 1. The Oscars shortlists will be revealed on Dec. 15, with 15 international films selected to be voted on by Academy members in all branches who commit to watch all 15 films. Oscar nominations will be revealed on Jan. 21. This year’s entries include titles like Romania’s “Fjord,” which won the Palme d’Or at Cannes; Chile’s “The Meltdown,” which screened in Un Certain Regard; and Germany’s “Everytime,” which won Cannes’ Un Certain Regard prize. Meanwhile, a new Academy rule allows any film that wins the top prize at one of the six biggest festivals — Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance, Busan and Toronto — to be entered in the international feature race even without a national committee’s backing. Gondhal (India) Image Credit: Davakhar Films The Film Federation of India has selected the Marathi-language drama “Gondhal” as the country’s entry for the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. Written and directed by Santosh Davakhar, the drama unfolds over a single night in rural Maharashtra, following a newlywed couple whose traditional wedding ritual becomes the setting where old customs, private desires and hidden fragility all come to a head. The cast includes Ishita Deshmukh, Yogesh Sohoni, Kishor Kadam, Suresh Vishwakarma, Nishad Bhoir, Anuj Prabhu and Vitthal Kale. “Gondhal” picked up a Golden Peacock nomination at the International Film Festival of India’s 56th edition, and Davakhar took home the event’s Silver Peacock for best director. The film later won a Fipresci prize when Bengaluru’s international film festival held its 17th edition, along with best director and best cinematographer honors from Pune’s international film festival and a further best director win at the Third Eye Asian International Film Festival. La Bola Negra (Spain) Image Credit: 'La Bola Negra' “La Bola Negra,” Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s Cannes Festival sensation, is Spain’s international feature Oscar submission. That comes as little surprise Scoring a 16-minute standing ovation at the Cannes Festival, where it shared its best director award “La Bola Negra” again moved waves when Netflix, its U.S. distributor, announced it would give “La Bola Negra” a 47-day U.S. theatrical window the longest for any movie in the streaming giant’s history, a sure indication that the film will feature strongly among the streamer’s awards priorities for the fall. “La Bola Negra” is already being talked up as a candidate for Oscar nomination in multiple other categories. Sweeping, unapologetically passionate and hugely ambitious, “La Bola Negra” braids three connected stories, each shot in different film registers, chronicling the travails and legacy of Spain’s gay experience in 1932, 1937 during the Spanish Civil War, and 2017. It picks up on the first four pages in an unfinished novel by legendary poet-playwright Federico García Lorca plus some of his nearly last poems. The film features a feisty turn from Penélope Cruz as a cabaret dancer and a cameo from Glenn Close as a modern-day hispanist, accompanying Spanish stars Miguel Bernardeau, Guitarricadelafuente, Milo Quifes and Carlos Gutiérrez in lead roles. Four Seasons in Java (Indonesia) Image Credit: Forka Films Indonesia has selected Kamila Andini ‘s “ Four Seasons in Java ” (“Empat Musim Pertiwi”) as its submission for the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. Written and directed by Andini and produced by Ifa Isfansyah for Forka Films, the film stars Putri Marino, Arya Saloka, Christine Hakim and Hana Malasan. The story centers on Pertiwi (Marino), a formerly incarcerated woman who comes back to a hometown that will not welcome her, pushing her to reckon with a painful personal history set against ongoing silence, violence and social division. Elements of mystery, magical realism and science fiction run through the psychological drama as it examines trauma, memory and what it takes to reclaim a sense of home and identity. The selection extends Andini’s run as one of Indonesian cinema’s most consistent presences on the international festival circuit. Her 2021 feature “Yuni” premiered at the Toronto Film Festival, where it won the Platform Prize, and went on to become Indonesia’s Oscars submission that year. Her film “Before, Now & Then” (Nana) played in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival, where Laura Basuki won the Silver Bear for best supporting performance. “Four Seasons in Java” had its world premiere in the Centrepiece program at the ongoing Toronto Film Festival and is set to screen at the Busan International Film Festival next month. It has also picked up a best cinematography nomination at the 2026 Asian Pacific Screen Awards. Silent Friend (Hungary) Image Credit: Courtesy of Films Boutique Ildikó Enyedi’s “Silent Friend” is Hungary’s submission for the 2027 Oscars in the best international feature film category. Enyedi’s “On Body and Soul,” which won Berlin’s Golden Bear, was Oscar nominated in the same category in 2018. “Silent Friend,” which stars Tony Leung Chiu-Wai, Luna Wedler, Enzo Brumm and Léa Seydoux, is a poetic exploration of the relationship between humans, plants and time. It received six awards at the 82nd Venice Film Festival, and was recently selected as one of five nominees for the FIPRESCI Grand Prix, recognizing the best films of the year. Filipiñana (Philippines) Image Credit: Kino Lorber Rafael Manuel ’s “ Filipiñana ” has been chosen as the official entry from the Philippines in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. The film is written and directed by Manuel and is distributed by Kino Lorber. The film is set against a backdrop of oppressive heat and drought. The narrative follows Isabel, a 17-year-old from the provinces of the Philippines, who gets a job at a prestigious golf resort. The cast includes Jorrybell Agoto, Carmen Castellanos, Teroy Guzman, Carlitos Siguion-Reyna, Isabel Sicat and Nour Houshmand. Executive produced by Chinese auteur Jia Zhangke, “Filipiñana” bowed in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it took home the World Cinema Dramatic Special Jury Award for Creative Vision. The film went on to make its European premiere in the Perspectives section of the Berlin Film Festival. The film’s festival run has continued to build momentum since. It played the San Francisco International Film Festival, picking up the New Directors Award, and the Independent Film Festival of Boston, where it won the Grand Jury Prize for Best Narrative Feature. “Filipiñana” also collected the Luna de València for Best Feature Film at the Cinema Jove International Film Festival. Elephants in the Fog (Nepal) Image Credit: Courtesy of UTN, Les Valseurs, DGS Nepal’s International Feature Film Selection Committee has chosen Abinash Bikram Shah’s “Elephants in the Fog” as the country’s entry for the 99th Academy Awards. The film marks Shah’s feature directorial debut and follows a Kinnar community in a Nepalese village fighting to protect itself. It premiered in the Un Certain Regard section of the Cannes Film Festival in May, where it won the section’s Jury Prize, and also picked up nominations for the Caméra d’Or and the Queer Palm. The cast is led by Pushpa Thing Lama, Deepika Yadav, Jasmine Bishwokarma, Aliz Ghimire and Dura Sanjay Kumar Gupta. The Oscars selection comes as “Elephants in the Fog” continues to expand its footprint in international markets. Sales company Best Friend Forever has closed deals in several territories, including MetFilm Distribution in the U.K., Filmin in Spain, Vedette in Benelux, Trigon in Switzerland, Lev Cinema in Israel, Jayantii in Australia, EFAR Films in India, PT Falcon in Indonesia and the Film Development Council of the Philippines, alongside an inflight deal with Silk Route. Those additions build on earlier deals covering France, Germany and Austria, Brazil and Nepal itself. The film is produced by Underground Talkies Nepal, Les Valseurs and Die Gesellschaft DGS. We Are All Strangers (Singapore) Image Credit: Giraffe Pictures “We Are All Strangers,” written and directed by Anthony Chen, has been selected as Singapore‘s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. Set in contemporary Singapore, the film centers on family relationships and unexpected life changes. It stars Chen’s frequent collaborators Yeo Yann Yann and Koh Jia Ler, with Andi Lim and Regene Lim rounding out the cast. Earlier this year, it became the first Singaporean film selected for the main competition at the Berlin Film Festival. “We Are All Strangers” completes Chen’s Growing Up trilogy, which began with “Ilo Ilo” in 2013 and continued with “Wet Season” in 2019. The two earlier films have collectively won more than 50 international accolades, including five Golden Horse Awards, along with “Ilo Ilo‘s” Caméra d’Or win at Cannes. Both films previously served as Singapore’s Oscars entries, at the 86th and 93rd Academy Awards respectively. No Paradise if You Are Killed By a Woman (Iraq) Image Credit: Courtesy True Colours Kurdish-Norwegian director Halkawt Mustafa’s “No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman,” a Hollywood-style thriller about a female Kurdish sniper who returns to Mosul to try and rescue her younger sister, has been selected by Iraq as the country’s official entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. “No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman” follows a female sniper named Vyan who returns to the battlefield she once escaped, driven by vengeance and by the desperate hope of rescuing her younger sister who is still imprisoned by ISIS. The thriller launched out-of-competition at the Venice Film Festival and also plays in Toronto. Avan Jamal (“The Exam”) stars as Vyan, alongside Norwegian actor Thorbjørn Harr. The film’s main cast also comprises Kanar Sarchl and Kader Jalal. Mustafa, who was born in Iraqi Kurdistan and fled to Norway as a child, wrote the film that is inspired by his encounter with a female Peshmerga sniper on the front line in 2014, according to a statement from the Norwegian Film Institute which supported the film’s production. The film was shot on location in Mosul, Iraq, “using the city’s real streets and surroundings to create the physical and emotional authenticity Mustafa felt could only be achieved there,” the statement noted. Mustafa previously directed the feature “El Clásico” and the documentary “Hiding Saddam Hussein” that was successfully released in movie theatres across the Arab world. “No Paradise” is produced by Halkawt Mustafa, Janne Hjeltnes and John M. Jacobsen for Hene Films in Norway, in co-production with La Media in Iraqi Kurdistan and The Chimney Pot in Sweden. Italy’s True Colours is handling international sales. Strawberries (Morocco) Image Credit: 'Strawberries' Courtesy Lucky Number Laila Marrakchi’s “Strawberries” (“La más dulce”), about a group of Moroccan seasonal laborers hired to pick strawberries in Spain who decide to stand up to their abusive employers, has been selected by the Moroccan Cinematographic Center as its official entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. Marrakchi, after portraying Morocco’s upper classes in “Marock” and “Rock the Casbah” (2013) – and then veering into TV by directing episodes of Damien Chazelle’s “The Eddy” for Netflix and of several French TV series including “The Bureau” – in “Strawberries” turns her eye to the true story of young women who leave Morocco for a strawberry farm in Southern Spain in hopes of providing a better life for their families, only to contend with harassment and inhumane living conditions. The female-driven drama, which is It is produced by France’s Lumen and Morocco’s Mont Fleuri Production with Spain’s Fasten Films and Belgium’s Mirage Films, launched earlier this year from Cannes’ Un Certain Regard. Lucky Number is handling international sales. Morocco has yet to score an Oscar nomination, though it has made the shortlist three times most recently in 2023 with Asmae El Moudir’s “The Mother of All Lies.” Tell Me Everything (Israel) Image Credit: Ziv Berkovich Moshe Rosenthal’s “Tell Me Everything” has been voted Best Picture at Israel’s Ophir Awards, automatically making it the country’s submission for best international feature film category at the 99th Academy Awards. “Tell Me Everything,” set in the 1980s against the rising HIV epidemic, premiered at Sundance in the world cinema dramatic competition. It is Moshe Rosenthal’s sophomore feature. “Karaoke,” his directorial feature debut, premiered at the 2022 Tribeca Film Festival. “Tell Me Everything” follows Boaz (played by Yair Mazor), a 12-year-old who discovers a devastating secret about his father. Catching up with Boaz as an adult (played by “The Vanishing Soldier’s” Ido Tako), the film delves into their father-son relationship as they attempt to heal wounds and repair bonds. Assi Cohen (“Yossi & Jagger”) stars as Boaz’s father. Fjord (Romania) Image Credit: Courtesy of Tudor Panduru “Fjord,” written and directed by Cristian Mungiu, is Romania’s submission for the 2027 Oscars in the best international feature film category, having been unanimously chosen by the country’s selection committee. The film premiered in the official competition at the Cannes Film Festival, where it won the Palme d’Or for best film, the FIPRESCI Prize, the Ecumenical Jury Prize, the Prix de la Citoyenneté and the François Chalais Prize. Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve star in the lead roles, with cinematography by Tudor Vladimir Panduru, editing by Mircea Olteanu, and production design by Simona Pădurețu. Aontas (Ireland) Image Credit: Púca Pictures “Aontas,” the Irish-language heist thriller from director Damian McCann, has been chosen as Ireland’s entry for the best international feature film category at the 2027 Academy Awards. The film was selected by the Irish Film & TV Academy (IFTA) and a committee including “Evil Dead Rise” director Lee Cronin, “Derry Girls” creator Lisa McGee, BAFTA-nominated director Brian Kirk (“Game of Thrones), BAFTA nominated director Kathryn Ferguson (“Nothing Compares”), Emmy-winning actress and filmmaker Aisha Tyler (“Friends”), actress Fionnuala Flaherty (“Kneecap”) and IFTA chief executive Áine Moriarty. Told in reverse chronology, “Aontas” follows three unlikely thieves, led by a woman on the verge of a breakdown, who rob a rural Irish bank. Opening in the tragic aftermath of the heist-gone-wrong. What starts as a poorly executed robbery becomes a portrait of a wilful woman trapped in her own past. It stars Carrie Crowley (“The Quiet Girl “), Bríd Brennan, Eva-Jane Gaffney, Seán T. Ó Meallaigh, Marcus Lamb and Art Parkinson. The Meltdown (Chile) Image Credit: 'The Meltdown' Courtesy of Mubi Chile’s Film Academy has selected “The Meltdown” (“El deshielo”) by Manuela Martelli, her post-Pinochet mystery drama set in an Andes ski resort, to represent the country in the Best International Feature category at the 2027 Academy Awards. Martelli’s follow-up to her acclaimed drama “Chile, 1976” had its world premiere at Cannes’ prominent strand Un Certain Regard this year. “The Meltdown” stars Maya O’Rourke – in her film debut – who plays a nine-year-old at her family’s ski resort who witnesses unsettling events that will test her loyalties. Other cast members are Paulina Urrutia, Mauricio Pešutić, Paula Zúñiga, Marcela Salinas and Lautaro Cantillana. All of a Sudden (Japan) Image Credit: Courtesy of Neon, Cannes Film Festival Hamaguchi Ryusuke‘s “All of a Sudden” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan (Eiren) has revealed. The selection marks the second time a Hamaguchi film has represented Japan in the category, five years after “Drive My Car” won the international feature Oscar and picked up nominations for best picture, director and adapted screenplay at the 94th Academy Awards. “All of a Sudden” is a France-Japan co-production made with backing from Germany and Belgium, shot largely in Paris. The film draws on “When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist,” a book of correspondence by Miyano Makiko and Isono Maho. It follows Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira), who runs a nursing home outside Paris and pushes to adopt a more dignity-focused model of elderly care, and Morisaki Mari (Okamoto Tao), a Japanese theater director undergoing cancer treatment. Nagatsuka Kyōzō and Kurosaki Kōdai round out the cast. Everytime (Germany) Image Credit: Courtesy of The Barricades Sandra Wollner’s “Everytime” has been selected as Germany’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film. The film’s synopsis reads as follows: The last photograph Jessie took shows the sun over Berlin. It hangs there as if nothing had happened. But Ella has lost her daughter. What remains is Jessie’s younger sister and a complicated relationship with the boy everyone blames. The unlikely trio ends up on a family holiday that never really existed. Under the shimmering sun of Tenerife, memory and the present become inseparably intertwined. The ghosts are everywhere. “Everytime” celebrated its world premiere at the 79th Cannes Film Festival in May. Wollner’s third feature film, for which she also wrote the screenplay, was selected for the Un Certain Regard sidebar where it won the Prix Un Certain Regard, the section’s top award. Cannes was followed by invitations to the Sydney Film Festival and the Karlovy Vary Film Festival, among others. At the Sarajevo Film Festival, “Everytime” was awarded the Heart of Sarajevo Grand Prize. Its North American premiere will follow in September at the Toronto Film Festival. Other festival appearances include the New York Film Festival. Becoming Human (Cambodia) Image Credit: Anti-Archive The Cambodia Oscar Selection Committee (COSC) has selected “Becoming Human,” directed by Polen Ly, as the country’s official submission for the international feature film category at the 99th Academy Awards. The film follows Thida, the spirit guardian of an aging cinema slated for demolition, as she weighs the choice of rebirth against her existence as a ghost. Her bond with Hai, a living man she meets along the way, pushes her to confront both her spiritual fate and a country in the midst of sweeping social change. “Becoming Human” is Ly’s debut feature. He previously made the short film “Further and Further Away” in 2022 and the documentary “Until the Orchid Blooms,” which premiered at IDFA in 2024 and won the grand prize at the Taiwan International Documentary Festival in 2026. The cast is led by 15-year-old newcomer and dance student Savorn Serak alongside Piseth Chhun, who won the Venice Horizons award for best actor in 2021 for his role in Kavich Neang’s “White Building.” First Light (Australia) Image Credit: International Film Festival Rotterdam “First Light,” the feature directorial debut of Filipino-Australian filmmaker James J. Robinson, has been selected as Australia’s entry in the international feature film category at the 99th Academy Awards, marking the first Filipino-Australian co-production and the first Tagalog-language film the country has ever submitted for Oscar consideration. The film follows Sister Yolanda (Ruby Ruiz), a nun and nurse leading a peaceful, disciplined existence until a young construction worker’s suspicious death draws her into uncovering corruption reaching both the community’s wealthy elite and the church she has devoted her life to. The film premiered at the 2025 Melbourne International Film Festival, where Robinson took home the best Australian director award. It later screened in the main competition lineup at Marrakech and went on to play the New Zealand International Film Festival, the International Film Festival Rotterdam and the Glasgow Film Festival. Possible Love (South Korea) Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix, Venice Film Festival The Korean Film Council (KOFIC) has selected “Possible Love,” directed by Lee Chang-dong, as South Korea‘s official entry for the international feature film category at the 2027 Academy Awards. “Possible Love” marks Lee’s first feature in eight years, following “Burning,” “Poetry” and “Secret Sunshine.” The film centers on two married couples whose lives intersect after a funeral: Mi-ok and her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu), who live quietly with their young son Cheol, and Ye-ji, a filmmaker making a documentary about workers who lost their jobs, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung). When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed by Ye-ji, the two women grow close, while Mi-ok finds herself unsettled by an attraction to Sang-woo. As the two couples’ worlds overlap, cracks begin to surface in both marriages. In its evaluation, the committee cited the film’s polished craftsmanship and the clarity of its directorial vision, pointing to the tone and mise-en-scène that sustain a sense of pressure throughout the story. The drama was described as prompting reflection on gentle forms of violence, incomplete freedom and the nature of true happiness, alongside a labor movement sequence that the committee said captured layered social undercurrents. Like a Limbless Tree (Turkey) Image Credit: Courtesy Tekhne Film “Like a Limbless Tree,” an intimate social drama directed by Tunç Davut, has been selected as Turkey‘s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film. Davut, whose previous works include the 2015 drama “Entanglement and TV series “Serçe” and “Kinali Kuzular,” delves into the fragility of human existence against a backdrop of the theme of immigration in “Like a Limbless Tree.” The film is produced by Istanbul-based Tekhne Film and stars Ali Ipin, Fayyaz Duman and Selen Kurtaran. Davut’s drama – which won an award at the Bosphorus Film Festival and was selected for the Antalya Golden Orange Film Festival and the Ankara Film Festival – is about a retired engineer named Refik whose life changes forever after being diagnosed with a terminal disease just as his Syrian caregiver disappears while attempting to flee to Europe, leaving him in charge of her two children. Who is Still Alive (Switzerland) Image Credit: Courtesy Swiss Films “Who is Still Alive,” a documentary directed by Nicolas Wadimoff that gives voice to Gaza humanitarian crisis survivors and refugees, has been selected by the Swiss Federal Office of Culture as Switzerland ‘s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film. The documentary, which looks at the lives of nine Palestinian people who escaped the crisis in Gaza and explores the loss of home against the backdrop of the Gaza War, had its world premiere in Venice at the 2025 Giornate degli Autori, AKA Venice Days, sidebar. For director Nicolas Wadimoff, “Who is Still Alive” is his third film dealing with Palestine, following “Aisheen (Still Alive in Gaza)” about the aftermath of Israel’s 2008 air strikes on the Gaza Strip and “The Apollo of Gaza” in 2018. “Who is Still Alive” was produced by Nicolas Wadimoff, Philippe Coeytaux, and Ketsia Stocker of the Geneva-based production company Akka Films, where Nicolas Wadimoff also serves as founder and producer. Co-producers include Easy Rider Films (Paris), Philistine Films (Palestine/Jordan), Cocoon Films (London), and RTS Radio Télévision Suisse. How to Divorce During the War (Lithuania) Image Credit: Courtesy of New Europe Film Sales Andrius Blaževičius’ “How to Divorce During the War” has been selected as Lithuania’s entry for the Academy Award for best international feature film. Blaževičius’ third feature won the directing award in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at the Sundance Film Festival. The film was picked up for theatrical distribution in North America by Zeitgeist Films, in association with Kino Lorber, and will be released on Aug. 21. Set in Vilnius in 2022, it’s a story of a high-flying executive Marija, who chooses the worst possible moment for an honest conversation with her husband Vytas about divorcing – just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine goes into full scale. Now the couple must navigate the process of separation as it collides with a refugee and mid-life crisis. Loading comments...
